description: Q2 FY2026 earnings review for an asset-light freight and contract-logistics operator.
provenance: Modeled on public earnings supplements from global freight-forwarding and contract-logistics companies: shipment volumes, yield, network utilization, business-line mix, cost actions, and forward guidance. Deliberately exercises an eight-slide deck with a multi-series line chart, pie chart, four operational KPIs, and region-specific commentary.

content.title: Network and customer highlights
content.subtitle: Execution across strategic verticals and trade lanes
bulletPoints: Won a five-year, $410M life-sciences control-tower mandate covering 23 countries; transition begins in October 2026
Opened the Monterrey cross-border campus at 82% pre-committed occupancy, adding 620K square feet of capacity
Asia-Europe ocean schedule reliability improved to 88% from 76% after carrier allocation was rebalanced in March
Top-25 customer retention was 100%; net revenue from those accounts increased 12% on automotive and healthcare growth
Digital booking penetration reached 74% of transactional shipments, reducing manual touches per file by 19%
Exited three subscale leased warehouses in the U.K.; $9M annualized savings expected from Q4 FY2026

content.title: Service gains are translating into durable share and margin.
content.subtitle: Henrik Dahl, Group Chief Executive
prose: Network reliability is winning time-sensitive healthcare and aerospace volume.
Automation and route density support further margin expansion.

content.title: FY2026 outlook
content.subtitle: Guidance updated August 12, 2026; assumes current fuel curves and FX rates
bulletPoints: Net revenue growth of 6%-8%, narrowed from 5%-9%, with transport volume growth in the mid-single digits
Adjusted EBIT of $555M-$585M, raised from $525M-$575M; H2 includes $12M of life-sciences transition costs
Free cash flow of at least $360M before acquisitions and shareholder distributions
Capital expenditure of $210M-$230M, primarily automation, cold-chain facilities, and the Monterrey campus
Year-end net leverage expected below 1.4x adjusted EBITDA after the September dividend payment
FY2027 planning assumption: ocean contract rates broadly stable with low-single-digit global capacity growth
